title: Dotted notes
summary: Add a dot to make a note half as long again, starting with the 3-beat minim.
usSummary: Add a dot to make a note half as long again, starting with the 3-beat half note.

hook.text: Walk, walk. Now hobble, as if your foot hurts: long, short, long, short. That uneven step is all over music. Press play and tap your foot steadily. Where does the tune start to hobble?

explore.text: Your turn. Count 1, 2, 3, 4 with the clicks. First tap on 1, hold for 3 clicks and tap on 4. Then hobble: tap on 1, then halfway between 2 and 3, then on 3 and 4.
explore.goal: Tap through all 4 [[bar|bars]]: the 3-click holds first, then the hobbles.

cards.text: That dot after a note is the key. A [[dotted-note|dotted note]] lasts half as long again. A [[minim|minim]] lasts 2 beats. Half of 2 is 1, so a dotted [[minim|minim]] lasts 3 beats: the note you held for 3 clicks.
A [[crotchet|crotchet]] lasts 1 beat. Half of 1 is ½, so a dotted [[crotchet|crotchet]] lasts 1½ beats. One [[quaver|quaver]] then fills the rest of the second beat: long, short. That is the hobble.

The dot adds half. Dotted [[minim|minim]]: 2 + 1 = 3 beats. Dotted [[crotchet|crotchet]]: 1 + ½ = 1½ beats. In 4/4 a dotted note must not start on beat 2: it would hide the middle of the [[bar|bar]]. Ties, in the next lesson, show the fix.

alternative.text: Count in halves: 1 and 2 and 3 and 4 and. A dotted [[crotchet|crotchet]] lasts 3 halves: say 1-and-2 and tap only on the 1. One [[quaver|quaver]] takes the next half. A dotted [[minim|minim]] lasts 6 halves: 1-and-2-and-3-and.

questions.prompt: How many beats does the dotted note last?
questions.hint: The dot adds half the note's own length. Work out half of the plain note first.

questions.prompt: Both clips tick at the same speed. Which one has the long-short hobble?
questions.hint: Tap a steady beat while you listen. Which clip has a long note followed by a short one?

options.reason: Clip B steps evenly, one note on every click. The long-short hobble is in clip A, where each long note is followed by a short one.

questions.hint: A dotted [[crotchet|crotchet]] lasts 1½ beats. Add up 1 + 1 + 1½. How much of the 4 is left?

questions.prompt: Every [[bar|bar]] here should hold 4 beats. One has too many. Tap it.
questions.hint: A dotted [[minim|minim]] is 2 beats plus half of 2. Count each [[bar|bar]].

payload.explanation: [[bar|Bar]] 3 has 5 beats: a dotted [[minim|minim]] (3) and a [[minim|minim]] (2). After a dotted [[minim|minim]] only 1 beat is left.

questions.prompt: Listen, then tap this rhythm. One tap for each note. A dotted note gets one tap.
questions.hint: Say "hob-ble" for a dotted [[crotchet|crotchet]] and one [[quaver|quaver]]: tap on "hob", then on "ble", half a beat after the dotted note ends.

questions.prompt: Tap this rhythm. One tap for each note.
questions.hint: A dotted [[crotchet|crotchet]] lasts a beat and a half: tap, then wait half a beat before the [[quaver|quaver]].
The dotted [[minim|minim]] fills a whole [[bar|bar]] of 3/4: tap on 1 and hold through 2 and 3.

questions.prompt: Match each symbol with how long it lasts.
questions.hint: A dot adds half. A [[crotchet|crotchet]] is 1 beat and a [[minim|minim]] is 2, so work out each dotted length first.

options.reason: That [[bar|bar]] hobbles on beat 1. In the clip beats 1 and 2 are even, and the long-short comes at the end.
That [[bar|bar]] steps evenly all the way through. The clip ends with a long note followed by a short one.

questions.prompt: Every [[bar|bar]] here should hold 4 beats. One has too few. Tap it.
questions.hint: A dotted [[crotchet|crotchet]] lasts 1½ beats. Add up each [[bar|bar]].

payload.explanation: [[bar|Bar]] 2 has 3½ beats: two [[crotchet|crotchets]] (2) and a dotted [[crotchet|crotchet]] (1½). It is ½ beat short.

questions.prompt: A dotted [[crotchet|crotchet]] is followed by one [[quaver|quaver]]. How many beats do the two notes last together?
questions.hint: A dotted [[crotchet|crotchet]] is 1½ beats. Each [[quaver|quaver]] is half a beat.

options.reason: That is the dotted [[crotchet|crotchet]] on its own. The [[quaver|quaver]] adds ½ beat more, so the two last 2 beats.
One [[quaver|quaver]] lasts half a beat, not a whole one. 1½ plus ½ is 2 beats.

points: A dot after a note makes it half as long again: the dot adds half the note's own length.
A dotted [[minim|minim]] lasts 3 beats (2 + 1). A dotted [[crotchet|crotchet]] lasts 1½ beats (1 + ½).
A dotted [[crotchet|crotchet]] and one [[quaver|quaver]] last 2 beats together. Say it as the hobble: long, short.
